exposure: premature rupture of membranes (>18 hours before labor)
cohort: The study included 422 preterm infants (28+0-36+6 weeks of gestational age), 330 of whom showed signs of histologic intrauterine infection, from a neonatal intensive care unit between June 2017 and June 2022.
finding: Histologic intrauterine infection is associated with higher complication and mortality rates, and increasing severity of inflammation, in preterm infants.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was associated with a higher incidence of histologic IUI, more severe inflammation, and a higher incidence of complications.
gest_age: 28+0-36+6 weeks of gestational age, with low gestational age associated with a higher incidence of histologic IUI, more severe inflammation, and a higher incidence of complications.
